articles.title: Canada’s language training sector in “state of crisis” after further enrolment declines in 2025
articles.summary: Languages Canada’s 2025 Annual Survey Report states that the country’s language training sector is in a “state of crisis” due to further enrolment declines in 2025. The report is based on responses from over 150 Canadian English and French language programmes that participated in both the 2024 and 2025 surveys.
articles.insight:
Canada’s language training sector crisis may reflect broader shifts in international student preferences, potentially indicating reduced interest in Canada as a study destination due to visa processing delays, cost-of-living pressures, or evolving perceptions of post-study work opportunities—though direct spillover to other countries remains uncertain without corroborating data from source markets.  
Admissions teams should monitor application trends from key Canadian feeder countries (e.g., India, Nigeria, Philippines), track comparative visa approval rates and processing times, and assess whether language test waivers or pathway partnerships need refinement to remain competitive amid changing enrolment patterns elsewhere.

articles.title: UK Home Office revokes Bloomsbury Institute’s student sponsor license
articles.summary: The UK Home Office has revoked Bloomsbury Institute’s student sponsor license, the most serious sanction available for licensed sponsors. This action means the institute can no longer sponsor international students to study in the UK.
articles.insight:
This revocation signals heightened UK regulatory scrutiny of student sponsors, potentially amplifying perceptions of visa risk among international applicants—though direct impact on overall demand remains uncertain without evidence of broader enforcement trends or shifts in source market sentiment.  
Admissions teams should monitor UK Home Office announcements and agent feedback for emerging concerns about compliance burdens or processing delays, while reviewing their own sponsorship practices and contingency plans for students considering multiple English-speaking destinations.

articles.title: HKDSE exam takers in mainland China face 220% jump in registration fee to HK$8,000
articles.summary: Students taking the HKDSE exam in mainland China next year will pay a registration fee of HK$8,000, representing a 220% increase from the current HK$2,500 following the end of a pilot scheme. Meanwhile, local Hong Kong students will face a 4% fee increase per subject, with charges ranging from HK$540 to HK$808.
articles.insight:
The sharp fee hike for HKDSE exams in mainland China may signal growing financial and logistical barriers for students seeking Hong Kong qualifications, potentially redirecting some toward alternative pathways—including undergraduate admissions in English-speaking countries—though demand shifts will depend on broader economic and policy trends.  
Admissions teams should track application volume and yield patterns from mainland China over the next 12–18 months, particularly among academically strong students previously targeting Hong Kong universities, while reviewing scholarship eligibility criteria to remain competitive amid rising education costs.

articles.title: Australian university wins Vietnam's first foreign branch campus license
articles.summary: RMIT Saigon South has been granted Vietnam’s first license for a foreign university branch campus. This authorization allows the institution to expand both its physical campus and its range of academic programs.
articles.insight:
RMIT’s milestone signals growing Vietnamese regulatory openness to foreign higher education, potentially reflecting rising domestic demand for internationally accredited degrees—but it remains unclear whether this will meaningfully divert students from traditional Anglophone destinations or instead expand overall outbound mobility.  
Admissions teams should track Vietnamese student application trends to their institutions over the next 12–18 months, particularly in STEM and business fields, while noting how RMIT Saigon South’s program offerings, tuition levels, and graduate outcomes evolve relative to regional alternatives.
